title: The Torn Rule · Part 2
idea: Two of you said SILENT: at 3:34 am you don't make a sound, and behind you someone answers the door in your voice ('Coming! Just a second!'); you live alone; an unknown number texts 'good, you stayed silent, now look at the roof'; the fox climbs down with her lantern and slides the other half of rule three under your back door: 'say nothing. The one who answers is not you.' Your own footsteps walk down the hall, the front door opens, the neighbors step aside and the tall shadow walks it into the dark. At 6 am: 'All clear. Thank you for your silence.' But how long had it been living with you?
hook: Two of you said SILENT. So at 3:34 am, you don't make a sound. Then, behind you, someone answers the door. In your voice.
caption:
Part 2. Two of you said SILENT. 🤫
So you didn't make a sound. Then, behind you, someone answered the door. In your voice.

The fox brought the other half of rule three. 🦊🏮
"If someone knocks three times, say nothing. The one who answers is not you."

You stayed silent. It walked out. But how long had it been living with you? Tell me in the comments 👇
